summary: Stafford already cost you the QB slot — 4.1 points, and Lawrence was on the bench. Lineup is otherwise right. The real move is a trade: Team 13 is starting Rachaad White at RB2 with Lamar Jackson rotting on their bench.

items.headline: Stafford busted and it is already banked
items.body: 155 yards, one interception, no touchdowns in a 27-7 loss in Melbourne; the Rams benched the starters late. 4.1 points from your QB slot, locked. Lawrence projected 16.0 at rank 8 on your bench. Start Lawrence from week 2 unless the matchup says otherwise.

items.headline: Trevor Lawrence is the QB going forward
items.body: Rank 8 among quarterbacks against Stafford's unranked, and Jacksonville is a 7.5-point home favorite over a Browns team with the worst line in football. Stafford is 38, coming off an MVP year built on a career-high 7.7% touchdown rate that will regress.

items.headline: Colston Loveland
items.body: Rome Odunze is day-to-day with a calf. If he sits, Loveland and Luther Burden absorb the target share in Ben Johnson's offense. Rank 2 at the position already.

items.headline: Tuten is a co-starter, not a lead back
items.body: Jacksonville lists Tuten and Chris Rodriguez as co-starters and the beat expects a near-even split. LeQuint Allen (hip) likely sits, which pushes receiving work to Tuten — worth more here at full PPR. He keeps the flex, but the lead-back premise is gone.

items.headline: Lloyd stays on the bench despite the higher projection
items.body: ESPN has him at 12.8 to Tuten's 12.0, but OC Adam Stenavich said plainly it will be committee 'for a little bit' across Lloyd, Chris Brooks and Kaleb Johnson. Lloyd has 10 career regular-season snaps. The projection is pricing a bell-cow role nobody has promised.

items.headline: Mayer is a hold, not a start — yet
items.body: Bowers had a meniscus trim on Sept 8 and is out one to two games; Mayer is the TE1 against Miami and Las Vegas just gave him three years and $45M. Ownership moved +1.56 in a day, the largest move on either roster. Loveland still outprojects him, so he sits this week — but do not drop him while Bowers is out.

items.headline: Jaguars D/ST
items.body: Consensus number-one defense of the week against Deshaun Watson and the worst offensive line in the league.

items.headline: You are heavily concentrated on Jacksonville
items.body: Tuten in the flex, Cam Little at kicker, the Jaguars defense, and Lawrence on the bench. A blowout win caps Little and Tuten's receiving work; a blowout loss craters the defense. Worth knowing before it happens, not after.
